newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Senior Pakistani police officer, driver shot dead.
newsitem.headline: Senior Pakistani police officer, driver shot dead.

text.p: Gunmen killed a senior police officer and his driver in the Pakistani city of Gujranwala in Punjab province on Tuesday, police said.
They said the unidentified attackers had ambushed senior superintendent of police Mohammad Ashraf Marth on his way to work in an official vehicle at about 8.45 a.m. (0345 GMT).
Marth, 35, and his driver Mohammad Tabassum died on the spot. The assailants, earlier reported to have been riding motorcyles, escaped in a car, police said.
They had no word on the motive for the attack, which occurred amid a surge in sectarian violence ahead of the Shi'ite Moslem mourning month of Muharram, which starts on Friday.
Two Shi'ite activists were shot dead on Monday, one in the provincial capital Lahore and one in the city of Faisalabad, bringing this year's sectarian death toll to about 70.

Most of the violence, involving tit-for-tat attacks by Sunni and Shi'ite militants, has taken place in populous Punjab province, where troops have been ordered to stand by to help civil authorities during Muharram.
Leaders of Sunni and Shi'ite religious parties, including several militant groups, met Punjab government officials on Monday and pledged to keep the peace during Muharram.

They agreed to a seven-point code of conduct to honour each other's beliefs, avoid criticism of other sects, preach unity and religious harmony, and tolerate processions and religious activities during Muharram and the Prophet's birthday.
The parties also pledged to help the administration and peace committees maintain law and order.
Participants included Azam Tariq, leader of the militant Sunni Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan group, and Allama Munawer, chief of the rival Shi'ite Sipah-i-Muhammad Pakistan faction.

Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif and his brother Shahbaz Sharif, who is chief minister of Punjab province, have sworn to stamp out sectarian violence, which has emerged as the main security challenge to his government since it took power in February.
Shi'ites make up an estimated 15 percent of Pakistan's mainly Sunni population of about 138 million.
